meta.statement: These five species are constructed for teaching purposes. They are botanically plausible but fictional: this meadow is a teaching model, not a real regional flora. Field marks are slightly exaggerated in the models so they stay readable at quadrat distance (documented in design/realism-matrix.md).

species.name: Meadow Butterweed
species.role: clumped, showy — the research-question target species
species.flower: one rounded button-like head per stem, 2–3 cm across, bright yellow, on a bare stalk
species.leaf: alternate, lance-shaped (2–3× longer than wide, pointed tip), toothed edge
species.habit: upright single stems in dense patches
fieldMarks: shape: upright single stem with one rounded drumstick-like flower head on top
size: 40–55 cm tall (knee height); flower head 2–3 cm across
leaf: alternate lance-shaped leaves with pointed tips along the stem
colour: bright yellow head (secondary cue — confirm with shape and size)
species.lookAlikeWarning: Blue Sedge also grows in patches, but it has no yellow head and its blades arch from the base.

species.name: Common Daisy-leaf
species.flower: small white button flowers 8–12 mm across, one or two per plant, held just above the leaves
species.leaf: all leaves in a basal rosette, round to spoon-shaped with blunt teeth
fieldMarks: shape: flat basal rosette (all leaves radiate from one point at ground level), tiny button flowers on short stalks
size: 8–15 cm tall (hand height); flowers under 1.5 cm across
leaf: round to spoon-shaped leaves with blunt teeth, no leaves on the flower stalk
colour: white flowers (secondary cue — confirm with the rosette shape and size)
species.lookAlikeWarning: Young Bunchgrass tufts also sit low, but their blades are narrow and folded, not round with teeth.

species.name: Blue Sedge
species.role: moisture-gradient species — follows the wet ground
species.distribution: gradient (inhomogeneous Poisson, intensity rises with soil moisture)
species.flower: no showy flowers; a small brownish spike of seed cases at the tip of some stems
species.leaf: narrow arching blades rising from the base, bluish-green, edges fine-toothed
species.habit: dense tufts in the wetter ground
fieldMarks: shape: fountain-like tuft of many narrow blades arching out from the base; triangular stem base (feels edged, not round)
size: 30–45 cm tall (mid-shin height); blades 2–4 mm wide
leaf: blades all from the base, no leaves on the stem; tiny brown spike at stem tips
colour: bluish-green blades (secondary cue — confirm with the tuft shape and blade width)
species.lookAlikeWarning: Bunchgrass is also a tuft, but it is stiffer, upright, and never bluish; Blue Sedge favours the wet low ground.

species.name: Tussock Bunchgrass
species.role: dense random background — the percent-cover estimation species
species.flower: tiny straw-coloured seed heads along the tips of some stems in summer
species.leaf: many thin, stiff, upright blades in a tight tussock; blades hair-like and often folded lengthwise
species.habit: tight upright tussocks covering much of the meadow
fieldMarks: shape: tight upright tussock (a mop of stiff blades from one point); never a flat rosette, never arching like a fountain
size: 25–35 cm tall; tussock 15–25 cm across; blades under 2 mm wide
leaf: blades hair-thin, stiff, often folded lengthwise, rough edges
colour: straw to dull green (secondary cue — confirm with the tussock shape and blade width)
species.lookAlikeWarning: Blue Sedge is the arching bluish tuft of the wet ground; Bunchgrass is stiff, upright, and everywhere.
species.countMethod: percent cover estimated in bands (0–5%, 5–25%, 25–50%, 50–100%) — too dense to count individuals

species.name: Fen Orchid
species.role: rare and clumped — the species sampling can miss
species.distribution: rare clumps (Thomas cluster process, very sparse)
species.flower: 6–12 tiny greenish flowers in a loose one-sided spike at the stem top; each flower under 5 mm
species.leaf: exactly two broad oval basal leaves lying flat on the ground, shiny, parallel-veined
species.habit: slender single stems in a few small colonies
fieldMarks: shape: slender bare stem with a loose one-sided spike of tiny flowers, and exactly two flat oval leaves at the base
size: 20–30 cm tall; flowers under 5 mm; basal leaves 3–5 cm long
leaf: two (never more) shiny oval basal leaves with parallel veins, flat on the ground
colour: greenish flowers (secondary cue — the two flat oval leaves are the reliable mark)
species.lookAlikeWarning: Butterweed is also a bare stem with basal leaves, but it has one big yellow round head and many lance-shaped stem leaves; the orchid's flowers are tiny and one-sided.
